newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish 1997 GDP to grow 5 pct - OECD.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish 1997 GDP to grow 5 pct - OECD.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Monday forecast Poland's real gross domestic product (GDP) to grow at around 5.5 percent in 1996 and slow to five percent growth in 1997.

"Although 1996 might witness a slight deceleration, an expansion on the order of 5.5 percent can still be considered as the mid-point of the range of likely outcomes," the OECD said in its second annual economic survey devoted to Poland.
"Beyond this year, output growth can be sustained around five percent provided that policies remain sufficiently supply-side friendly and that external demand does not weaken too much," it said.
Poland's GDP grew by 7.0 percent last year and by 5.2 percent in 1994.

The Paris-based organisation, affiliating the world's 27 most developed economies, said the high rate of investment growth in Poland in recent years -- 18.5 percent in 1995 and a 19.5 percent growth forecast for this year -- suggested that a slowdown in economic growth was likely be limited.
The OECD predicted that Poland's inflation would fall to around 18 percent at the end of 1996 and 14 percent at the end of 1997, from 19.5 percent in October and 21.6 percent at the end of 1995.
It said it expected the unemployment rate to decline very gradually to around 13 percent at the end 1997, from 13.5 percent in September this year.
Poland was invited to become the OECD's 28th member earlier this year.
